title: Judaea, Galilee & Egypt
subtitle: Rulers and lands named in Matthew 2

items.text: Herod I (“the Great”), king of Judaea under Rome, reigned c. 37–4 BC. His death is most commonly dated to 4 BC.
A son of Herod. Ruled Judaea, Samaria and Idumaea as ethnarch c. 4 BC – AD 6, when Augustus removed him. This is his only appearance in Scripture.
The southern hill country, containing Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
The northern region, containing Nazareth. After Herod’s death it was governed separately from Judaea, by Herod Antipas.
A Roman province from 30 BC. Matthew does not name a city there.

sources: Historical dates follow Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, books 17–18, as summarised in standard reference works. Distances are straight-line, computed from the coordinates in this edition.
